summary: MARSIS (Mars Autonomous Research & Survival Intelligence System) is an AI-powered planetary exploration platform that transforms complex Martian scientific data into actionable mission intelligence. It integrates topographic, radiation, chemical, atmospheric, geological, optical, spectral, and thermal datasets into an interactive multilayer map. Using AI-driven analysis and Dijkstra's pathfinding algorithm, MARSIS identifies optimized routes based on mission objectives, terrain conditions, and environmental hazards. It evaluates route safety, highlights hazardous and safe segments, explains identified risks, and generates mission overviews covering estimated fuel consumption, elevation changes, and terrain difficulty. MARSIS aims to support safer, smarter, and more informed robotic and future human exploration of Mars.
details:
1. Multilayer Planetary Intelligence

The platform integrates multiple categories of Martian data into an interactive map, including:

  • Topographic data: Surface elevation, terrain structure, and slope variations.
  • Radiation data: Environmental radiation conditions and potential exposure risks.
  • Chemical data: Surface composition and chemical characteristics.
  • Atmospheric data: Atmospheric conditions and environmental factors.
  • Geological data: Surface formations and geological features.
  • Optical and spectral data: Surface imagery and material identification.
  • Thermal data: Surface temperature variations and thermal conditions.

2. Intelligent Route Optimization

MARSIS uses Dijkstra's shortest-path algorithm alongside AI-driven analysis to evaluate potential routes across the Martian surface. Route selection considers mission objectives, terrain characteristics, environmental conditions, and safety constraints rather than simply selecting the shortest distance.

3. Safety and Hazard Assessment

MARSIS evaluates the proposed journey and identifies safe and potentially hazardous route segments. Instead of providing only a general safety score, it explains which conditions create risks, where they occur, and why certain segments may be unsuitable for the mission.

4. AI-Powered Mission Overview

Every proposed journey is accompanied by an intelligent mission assessment covering estimated fuel consumption, elevation changes, terrain difficulty, environmental conditions, and overall route suitability.

Innovation and Impact

MARSIS brings multiple scientific data layers together into one mission-oriented decision-support system. Its key innovation is connecting planetary data visualization with route optimization, environmental risk assessment, and mission resource analysis.

The intended impact is to help researchers, mission planners, and future robotic and human exploration teams make more informed decisions when navigating the Martian surface.

Technology

MARSIS combines artificial intelligence, geospatial data visualization, planetary datasets, and graph-based pathfinding. Its architecture is designed to transform complex scientific information into understandable and actionable exploration insights.
